A Chinese programme to build and finance ports, railways, roads, pipelines and power plants abroad, announced by Xi Jinping in 2013. He set out a land "belt" through Central Asia in a speech in Kazakhstan and a sea "road" through Southeast Asia in Indonesia. The name calls up the old Silk Road.

More than a hundred countries signed on. Projects on the chart include:

  • the Laos to China railway
  • the Mombasa to Nairobi railway
  • the Jakarta to Bandung high-speed rail
  • the Central Asia to China gas pipeline

Chinese banks lent the money, Chinese firms often did the building, and China gained trade routes, markets for its steel and cement, and influence. Critics point to debt troubles in some borrowers; Sri Lanka leased the port of Hambantota to a Chinese company in 2017 after struggling to repay. Supporters say it built infrastructure that others would not fund. It recalls China's earlier aid in building TAZARA in the 1970s.
